keywords: Newton's Laws 2.Work 3.Mechanical Energy 4.Rotational Motion 5.Motion of Rigid Body
educationalGoal: In this course, students learn the basics of physics, such as description of motion, equations of motion for mass points and rigid bodies, work and energy, using vectors, differentiation and integral. In addition, the goal is to develop the ability to gain insight into the physics behind natural phenomena by applying the knowledge they have learned and through logical thinking and data analysis.
advice: Logical thinking and data analysis are conducted based on actual measurement data, and the ability to gain insight into the physics behind natural phenomena is nurtured. We will cover the following topics: 1. Dimension and units. 2. Motion in one dimension. 3. Motion in two dimensions. 4. Newton's laws of motion. 5. Energy of a system. 6. Conservation of energy. 7. Rotational motion. 8. Oscillatory motion. Students are required to have a knowledge of vectors, differentiation, and integration. Students will learn a number of formulas related to the laws of physics. Students will not only be expected to memorize the formulas but also be required to understand the meaning of these formulas.

requiredKnowledge: Background knowledge: Basic knowledge of elementary mathematics such as trigonometric ratios, vectors, differentiation, integration, etc. Skills: Trigonometric ratios, vectors, differentiation, integration, etc., elementary mathematics calculation skills

activityGoals.body: Basic knowledge of mechanics such as speed, acceleration, and force.
Ability to evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton’s equations of motion.
Ability to calculate potential energy using integral calculus and a knowledge of work and energy.
Ability to evaluate the rolling motion of a rigid object by deriving and solving relevant equations.
Ability to understand basic physics vocabulary and phrases.
Ability to understand the content of the lesson by completing the homework and paticipating in group activities.

achievementLevels.ideal: Accurately calculate position, velocity, and acceleration using appropriate mathematical formulas. Accurately evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton's equations of motion. Accurately calculate potential energy using integral calculus based on a knowledge of work and energy. Accurately evaluate the rolling motion of a rigid object by deriving and solving the equations of rolling motion. Understand basic physics vocabulary phrases and use them. Make a strong effort to understand the content of the lesson, and play a leading role in group activities.
achievementLevels.standard: Calculate position, velocity, and acceleration using appropriate mathematical formulas. Evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton's equations of motion. Calculate potential energy using integral calculus based on a knowledge of work and energy. Evaluate the rolling motion of a rigid object by deriving and solving the equations of rolling motion. Unserstabd basic physics vocabulary and phrases. Make a effort to understand the content of the lesson, and actively participate in group activities.

lessons.content: Course introduction Dimension and units Motion in one dimension (Average velocity, Instantane-ous velocity, Acceleration, Freely falling object)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Units of length, mass, and time and definitions of average velocity, instantaneous velocity, and acceleration Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Motion in two dimensions position vector, velocity vector, acceleration vector, projectile motion, uniform circular motion)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Definitions of position vector, velocity vector, acceleration vector, and how to calculate horizontal range and maximum height of a projectile Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: The laws of motion (the concept of force, Newton's laws)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Newton's laws Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: More applications of Newton’s laws (forces of friction, circular motion model, motion in the presence of velocity-dependent resistive force)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Difference between static friction and kinetic friction and how to calculate a central acceleration Review: Examples handled in class and related

lessons.content: Energy of a system (systems and Environments, work, conservative and nonconservative forces, potential energy)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Systems and environments and definitions of work, conservative forces and potential energy Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Quiz 1 on contents learned in #1-#5 Conservation of energy (conservation of mechanical energy, changes in mechanical energy for nonconservative forces)
lessons.assignments: Prepare for quiz 1 Preview: Conservation of mechanical energy and definition of power Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Group activity related to contents learned in #1-#6
lessons.assignments: Prepare for group activity Writing a report

lessons.content: Momentum and collisions (momentum, collisions, center of mass, motion of a system of particles)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Definition of momentum and impulse- momentum theorem Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Rotational motion (angular speed, angular acceleration, rigid object under constant angular acceleration, rotational kinetic energy, torque)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Definition of momentum and impulse- momentum theorem Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Rotational motion (rigid object in equilibrium, angular momentum, rolling motion of rigid objects)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Rigid object in equilibrium and definition of angular momentum Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Oscillatory motion (motion of an object attached to a spring, simple harmonic oscillation)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Definitions of amplitude, angular frequency, period, and frequency of simple harmonic oscillation Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Quiz 2 on contents learned in #6-#11 Oscillatory motion (pendulum, damped oscillations)
lessons.assignments: Prepare for quiz 2 Preview: Formulas related to simple harmonic oscillation Review: Examples handled in class and related objective questions

lessons.content: Group activity related to contents learned in #8-#12
lessons.assignments: Prepare for group activity Writing a report

lessons.content: Review for final exam Final exam of contents learned in #1-#13
Group activity Return of final exam paper and review Self-evaluation
lessons.operation: Group activity (as necessary), review, self-check, and self-evaluation
